name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Refund request gate (new, not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Refund request webhook
nodes.notes: 06's audit-gap list: 'refund gate.' Called by whatever initiates a refund conversation (a rep via a future Deals Desk UI action, a support-ticket intake workflow once W6.x is built) with {opportunityId, contractId (nullable), requestedAmountCents, reason, requestedByEmail}. This workflow is a GATE, not a processor - it never calls Stripe's refund API and never writes a 'refunded' status anywhere. It only logs the request durably and puts it in front of a human. Deliberately NOT built on the ai_action_requests table (command-center/src/messaging/db.ts) - that table is specifically the AI-employee human-approval queue (Tag-for-Action's human-to-AI half); a refund request isn't an AI action awaiting approval, it's a human business decision that was never going to be automated in the first place, so it gets its own durable log (Activity Event) instead.

nodes.name: Fetch Opportunity
nodes.notes: Only for companyName context in the alert/notification below - this workflow never writes back to the Opportunity itself. A refund is a Contract/BillingPeriod-level financial event, not a stage change, and CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md doesn't define a refund-specific Opportunity field.

nodes.name: Log to Activity Event

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ opportunityId: $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId, type: 'RefundRequested', contractId: $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.contractId || null, requestedAmountCents: $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.requestedAmountCents, note: $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.reason, by: $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.requestedByEmail, at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: Same /rest/activityEvents shape dnc-check.workflow.json's override log already uses ('Log override to Activity Event') - the durable, permanent record that a refund was requested, who requested it, and why. Nothing about this record implies approval or completion; it's a paper trail, not a transaction.

nodes.name: Notify accounting

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ recipientEmail: $env.ACCOUNTING_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL || 'PLACEHOLDER_ACCOUNTING_EMAIL', summary: 'Refund requested for ' + (($('Fetch Opportunity').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity').item.json).companyName || 'unknown company') + ': $' + (($('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.requestedAmountCents || 0) / 100).toFixed(2) + ' - ' + $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.reason, linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: Same personal-notification pattern tag-for-action.workflow.json's 'Notify human target' uses, reusing the Command Center Alerts Ingest credential (ALERTS_INGEST_SECRET) - Command Center's routes.ts trusts /api/notifications the same as /api/alerts. ACCOUNTING_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL is a new env var, not previously used anywhere in this repo - who actually processes refunds isn't specified by the brief, so this is a single named recipient rather than a channel, matching Tag-for-Action's own 'personal notification' delivery for a decision that needs one accountable owner.

nodes.name: Alert: refund requested

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'warning', source: 'refund-request', message: (($('Fetch Opportunity').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity').item.json).companyName || 'unknown company') + ' requested a refund of $' + (($('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.requestedAmountCents || 0) / 100).toFixed(2) + ' - ' + $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.reason + '. No refund has been processed; a human must action this.', linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Refund request webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: Routes to #accounting - alertRouting.ts's accounting route now matches 'refund' alongside 'contract-amendment'/'billing-period' (command-center/src/messaging/alertRouting.ts, edited this pass). Fans out from 'Log to Activity Event' in parallel with 'Notify accounting' and 'Respond: logged' - three independent branches off the same durable write, same fan-out shape as 'Advance Opportunity to Won' in stripe-payment-to-crm.workflow.json (one response node among several parallel branches, never gated behind the fire-and-forget ones, so the webhook caller isn't left waiting on - or double-responded to by - branches that don't affect what gets returned).

nodes.name: Respond: logged

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, logged: true, refunded: false, note: 'Request logged and routed to a human for review. No refund has been processed by this workflow.' }) }}

nodes.notes: refunded:false is explicit, not just an absent field - whatever calls this webhook should never mistake 'the gate accepted the request' for 'the refund happened.'
